1. Survodutide comes from Boehringer Ingelheim. It licenses the drug from Zealand Pharma and leads its development worldwide.
  2. Eloralintide comes from Eli Lilly. It is the same company behind tirzepatide and retatrutide.
  3. Neither is approved. Both are still investigational drugs, with no approval from the FDA, BPOM or any other regulator.
  4. Survodutide is closer to filing. Its phase 3 trials have reported, and Boehringer says it is preparing regulatory submissions for obesity. Eloralintide’s phase 3 trials only started in late 2025.

Survodutide and eloralintide are two of the newer names in weight-management research. They work in different ways: survodutide acts on the glucagon and GLP-1 receptors, while eloralintide copies the hormone amylin.

Below, we explain who makes each drug, how far each has come in clinical trials, and why neither can be prescribed yet.

Survodutide and Eloralintide at a Glance

Here is how the two drugs compare as of November 2026:

Survodutide Eloralintide
Developer Boehringer Ingelheim, licensed from Zealand Pharma Eli Lilly
Type of drug Glucagon/GLP-1 dual agonist Selective amylin receptor agonist
How it is given Once-weekly injection Once-weekly injection
Trial stage Phase 3 obesity trials reported in 2026 Phase 3 obesity trials started in late 2025
Best weight loss reported Up to 16.6% at 76 weeks (phase 3, without diabetes) Up to 20.1% at 48 weeks (phase 2)
Approved anywhere? No No

The weight-loss figures come from different trial phases, lengths and groups of people, so they are not a head-to-head comparison.

Who Makes Survodutide?

Survodutide was discovered by Zealand Pharma, a Danish biotech company, and is licensed to Boehringer Ingelheim. Boehringer, a German drug maker, is solely responsible for developing and selling it worldwide. During development, it carries the research code BI 456906.

A Glucagon and GLP-1 Dual Agonist

Survodutide acts on two hormone receptors. The GLP-1 part reduces appetite and slows digestion, as semaglutide does. The glucagon part works on the liver and on how much energy the body uses, which is why survodutide is also being studied for fatty liver disease. Retatrutide uses the glucagon receptor in a similar way, and we explain how retatrutide works in our guide to that drug.

Survodutide Phase 3 Results

Survodutide is in the late stage of phase 3. In SYNCHRONIZE-1, 725 adults without diabetes lost up to 16.6% of their body weight over 76 weeks, compared with 3.2% on placebo. In SYNCHRONIZE-2, 755 adults with type 2 diabetes lost up to 13.1%, compared with 3.1%, with better blood sugar control. Stomach side effects were the most common, and about 18% to 19% of people stopped treatment because of them, compared with 1% to 3% on placebo.

On 9 November 2026, Boehringer reported that survodutide did not raise the risk of heart attacks, strokes and other major heart events in a 5,530-person cardiovascular safety trial. The company says it is now moving forward with preparations for regulatory submissions in obesity.

Who Makes Eloralintide?

Eloralintide is developed by Eli Lilly, the maker of tirzepatide (sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound). Its research code is LY3841136.

A Selective Amylin Receptor Agonist

Eloralintide copies amylin, a hormone your pancreas releases with insulin after meals. Amylin helps you feel full and slows how quickly food leaves your stomach. Unlike survodutide, eloralintide does not act on the GLP-1 receptor at all. Lilly describes it as selective because it is designed to target the amylin receptor specifically.

Eloralintide Phase 2 Results and Phase 3 Plans

Eloralintide is earlier in development than survodutide. In a phase 2 trial of 263 adults with obesity or overweight, published in The Lancet in November 2025, people lost between 9.5% and 20.1% of their body weight over 48 weeks, depending on the dose, compared with 0.4% on placebo. The most common side effects were mild to moderate stomach symptoms and tiredness.

Lilly began enrolling phase 3 trials at the end of 2025. They are testing eloralintide on its own for obesity, including in people with type 2 diabetes and in people with higher heart risk, as well as for sleep apnoea and knee osteoarthritis pain.

Why Are Survodutide and Eloralintide Not Approved Yet?

Both drugs are still going through the steps every new medicine must complete before a doctor can prescribe it. Strong trial results are an important step, but they are not an approval.

First, the phase 3 trials have to finish and report. Survodutide has reached this point for obesity, while eloralintide’s phase 3 trials only began enrolling at the end of 2025. Next, the developer submits the full data package to regulators such as the US Food and Drug Administration. The regulator then reviews the safety, effectiveness and manufacturing data before deciding, and only then is an official label with approved uses and doses written.

Neither company has announced a filing date or an expected approval date. Approval also happens country by country, so even after an FDA decision, each drug would need its own BPOM registration before it could be prescribed in Indonesia.

Are Survodutide and Eloralintide Available in Bali?

Not as medicines. Neither drug is approved, so no doctor can prescribe them and no pharmacy can dispense them. Both are available in Bali as research compounds, supplied for laboratory and research use.

Survodutide for Research

We supply survodutide in Bali as a research compound. Our survodutide is sold for research use only. It is not a Boehringer Ingelheim product, it is not a BPOM-registered medicine, and it is not approved for human use.

Eloralintide for Research

We also supply eloralintide in Bali on the same basis. Our eloralintide is sold for research use only. It is not a Lilly product, it is not a BPOM-registered medicine, and it is not approved for human use.

Conclusion

Survodutide is made by Boehringer Ingelheim under licence from Zealand Pharma, and eloralintide is made by Eli Lilly. Survodutide is a glucagon/GLP-1 dual agonist that has completed its main phase 3 obesity trials and a heart safety trial, and Boehringer is preparing to file. Eloralintide is a selective amylin receptor agonist that showed up to 20.1% weight loss in phase 2 and entered phase 3 at the end of 2025.

Neither drug is approved anywhere yet, and neither company has announced an approval date. Until then, both are available in Bali only as research compounds, supplied for research use only.

Frequently Asked Questions

What Is Eloralintide?

Eloralintide is an investigational once-weekly injection from Eli Lilly that copies the hormone amylin. It is a selective amylin receptor agonist being tested for weight management, and it is not approved yet.

What Is Survodutide?

Survodutide is an investigational once-weekly injection that acts on the glucagon and GLP-1 receptors. Boehringer Ingelheim develops it under licence from Zealand Pharma, and it is not approved yet.

Is Survodutide Approved by the FDA?

No. Survodutide has finished its main phase 3 obesity trials, and Boehringer says it is preparing regulatory submissions, but no filing or decision date has been announced.

When Will Eloralintide Be Approved?

No date has been announced. Its phase 3 trials began at the end of 2025, so results, a filing and a regulatory review all still lie ahead.

Is Eloralintide the Same as Cagrilintide?

No. Both copy amylin, but they are different molecules from different companies. Cagrilintide is from Novo Nordisk and is combined with semaglutide in CagriSema, while eloralintide is Lilly’s own amylin drug.

Is Survodutide Stronger Than Tirzepatide?

There is no head-to-head trial to say. Survodutide reached up to 16.6% weight loss in its phase 3 trial without diabetes, but trials of different drugs used different people and lengths, so the figures cannot be compared directly.
